title: Container image and deployment
lead: Build a container image, a compose file and a backup procedure for the chosen host (ADR 0021; see "WSGI server" in docs/open-questions.md).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** distributable packaging for other households (Later); the proxy-trust and bootstrap fixes (S63); a scheduler (S64).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: larder has to run unattended for years on a home server.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. WSGI server: waitress (pure Python, no dependencies of its own) (recommended) or gunicorn? This is a new dependency, so it needs approval.
2. Base image (e.g., official `python:<ver>-slim`)? Image registry: build locally on the host (recommended) or push to a registry?
3. How should the deploy key and other secrets get onto the data volume?

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_wsgi_entrypoint_creates_app` (unit)
2. `test_wsgi_entrypoint_skips_bootstrap_and_starts_the_scheduler_once` (unit; S63, S64)
3. Container smoke: `/healthz` returns ok in the built image (scripted check)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Multi-stage build; non-root user; data volume at `/data`; healthcheck.
2. Compose: larder service + the reverse proxy from ADR 0021; no published ports beyond the proxy.
3. Startup: run `python -m larder bootstrap` once before the server (S63). The WSGI entrypoint calls `create_app(settings, bootstrap=False)` and starts S64's scheduler. No scheduler is chosen here.
4. Backups: SQLite `.backup` to a file on a schedule + data volume snapshot per ADR 0021; write a restore procedure and test it once.
5. Upgrade procedure: pull, build, migrate on start.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - The image builds; the container smoke check passes; a restore from backup works on a scratch volume.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
